title: On mobile the filter chips sit in a horizontally scrollable row below the tabs, starting with All Filters
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device (or a mobile-size browser window).
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
steps: 1. Look at the row below the tab row (All, Estimates, Completed, My Work Orders).
2. Swipe the chip row sideways.
expected: 1. A filter chip row is shown below the tabs, starting with an 'All Filters' chip (with a funnel icon) followed by the individual filter chips (Status, Customer, Lead Technician, ...).
2. The row scrolls horizontally - chips that do not fit are reachable by swiping.
3. A right-edge arrow affordance indicates the row can be scrolled (per the design variant).
notes: The scroll-arrow overlay appears in one design variant (11884:20807) - VIU-confirm whether the build shows it always, on overflow only, or not at all.

title: Tapping All Filters opens a bottom sheet listing every filter as an expandable row with an Apply filters button
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
steps: 1. Tap the 'All Filters' chip.
2. Read the sheet from top to bottom.
expected: 1. A bottom sheet slides up with a drag handle at the top, the centered title 'All Filters' and a close (x) button.
2. It lists the five filters as expandable accordion rows, each with its icon, name and a down arrow: Status, Customer, Lead Technician, Service Advisor, Asset on site.
3. A sticky blue 'Apply filters' button sits at the bottom of the sheet.
notes: DESIGN TYPO FLAG: the sheet rows in the design read 'Lead Tehnician' (missing 'c') - the build must ship 'Lead Technician' (design-notes C.1); if it inherits the typo, raise a bug.

title: Selecting statuses in the mobile sheet and tapping Apply filters filters the list and counts on the sheet title
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab; work orders exist in several statuses.
3. The 'All Filters' bottom sheet is open.
steps: 1. Tap the Status accordion row to expand it.
2. Tick one or more statuses.
3. Tap the 'Apply filters' button.
4. Reopen the All Filters sheet and look at its title.
expected: 1. Expanding Status reveals the same nine status checkboxes as desktop (Estimate, Approved, In progress, Review, Complete, Invoiced, Paid, Declined, Imported) plus 'Clear selection'.
2. After 'Apply filters' the sheet closes and the work order list shows only the ticked statuses.
3. The reopened sheet's title shows the applied-filter count, for example 'All Filters (1)', and the Status accordion header is highlighted with the selected values ticked.
spec_ref: requirements.md Story 12 S12-R2; S12-R3; Story 2 S2-R1
notes: Mobile uses an explicit 'Apply filters' step (unlike desktop's real-time filtering) - the sheet button is in the final design; VIU-confirm whether the list also live-updates before Apply.

title: Tapping an individual filter chip on mobile opens that filter's own sheet with an 'Apply filter' button
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
steps: 1. Tap the Status chip (not All Filters).
2. Read the sheet.
3. Tick a status and tap the bottom button.
expected: 1. A bottom sheet opens for that single filter: its title row shows the filter's icon and name (for example 'Status') with a close (x) button - no accordion list of the other filters.
2. The sheet shows only that filter's options (the nine status checkboxes plus 'Clear selection').
3. The bottom button reads 'Apply filter' (singular); tapping it applies the selection and filters the list.

title: The mobile Customer filter has search, multi-select and removable tags, matching desktop
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device.
2. You are on the Work Orders page; several customers exist.
3. The All Filters sheet is open with the Customer accordion expanded.
steps: 1. Type part of a customer name in the 'Search customer' field and watch the list.
2. Select two or three customers.
3. Look at the input area and the list rows.
4. Remove one customer with the x on its tag, then tap 'Apply filters'.
expected: 1. The list narrows to matching names as you type.
2. Each selected customer appears as a tag with an x in the input area, and its list row shows a checkmark.
3. Removing a tag deselects just that customer.
4. After 'Apply filters' the list shows only work orders of the remaining selected customers, and the sheet title counts the applied filters (for example 'All Filters (2)').

title: The mobile Lead Technician and Service Advisor filters offer their search lists in the sheet
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device.
2. You are on the Work Orders page; technicians and advisors exist.
3. The All Filters sheet is open.
steps: 1. Expand the Lead Technician accordion row and look at its content.
2. Collapse it, expand the Service Advisor row and look at its content.
3. Select one name in either list and tap 'Apply filters'.
expected: 1. The Lead Technician row opens with a 'Search technician' field and the technician list.
2. The Service Advisor row opens with a 'Search advisor' field and the advisor list.
3. Applying a selection filters the work order list just like on desktop.
spec_ref: requirements.md Story 12 S12-R2; Story 4 S4-R1; Story 5 S5-R1
notes: DESIGN TYPO FLAG: the accordion row label in the design reads 'Lead Tehnician' - the build must ship 'Lead Technician' (design-notes C.1).

title: The mobile Asset on site filter offers Yes/No with Clear selection in the sheet
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device.
2. You are on the Work Orders page; work orders exist in both on-site states.
3. The All Filters sheet is open.
steps: 1. Expand the Asset on site accordion row.
2. Choose Yes and tap 'Apply filters'.
3. Look at the list.
expected: 1. The Asset on site row opens showing the two options Yes and No plus 'Clear selection'.
2. Only one option can be selected at a time.
3. After applying, the list shows only work orders matching the chosen on-site state.

title: Active chips and Clear filters behave on mobile the same way as on desktop
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with at least one filter applied via the sheet.
steps: 1. Look at the chip row after applying the filter.
2. Look for a 'Clear filters' control while a filter is active.
3. Use it and look at the chips and the list.
expected: 1. The chip for the applied filter shows the active state with the selected value(s), like on desktop.
2. A 'Clear filters' control appears while at least one filter is active.
3. Using it removes all active filters, the chips return to default and the full list comes back.
spec_ref: requirements.md Story 12 S12-R2; Story 7 S7-R1/R3; Story 8 S8-R1
notes: The final mobile frames show the chip row unselected; the exact mobile placement of 'Clear filters' is not drawn - VIU-confirm where it appears (chip row vs sheet).

title: Mobile has no collapse toggle: the filter chip row is always visible
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
steps: 1. Look at the toolbar row (Search, sort icon, New Work Order button).
2. Look for any control that would hide the filter chip row.
expected: 1. There is no filter-bar collapse/expand (funnel) toggle on mobile.
2. The filter chip row is always visible on the mobile Work Orders page.
design_ref: design-notes.md B.1 #13 (11857:31046 - toolbar has Search, sort and New Work Order only)

title: Filters matching no work orders on mobile show the same empty state as desktop
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a mobile device.
2. You are on the Work Orders page; work orders exist.
steps: 1. Apply a filter combination that matches no work orders (for example a customer plus a status that customer never has).
2. Look at the list area.
expected: 1. The list shows the same no-results empty state as desktop, saying no results were found for the current filters.
2. The empty state includes the prompt to clear filters.
3. No error appears.
design_ref: design-notes.md B.1 (empty state not drawn in the final mobile frames)
notes: Exact mobile empty-state text is not in the design set - VIU-confirm it matches desktop.

title: The work order list request carries the active filter selections
permissions_required: A valid signed-in session; browser developer tools or an API client.
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser with developer tools open on the Network tab.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with no filters applied.
steps: 1. Apply a Status selection and a Customer selection in the filter bar.
2. In the Network tab, find the work order list request the page sends after the change.
3. Inspect the request's parameters.
expected: 1. The list request includes the active filter selections as request parameters (status values and customer identifiers).
2. The request succeeds (HTTP 200).
3. The response contains only work orders matching the filters - the filtering is done by the backend, not just hidden client-side.
design_ref: requirements.md Story 11 (URL state implies parameterized list requests)
spec_ref: requirements.md Story 2 S2-R2; Story 3 S3-R6 (backend view)
notes: The filters endpoint and parameter names are not in the spec (OQ-7) - capture the real endpoint shape live at VIU and tighten this case's wording then. If filtering turns out to be purely client-side in the build, flag it to the developers instead of failing blindly.

title: A combined multi-filter request returns only work orders matching all filters, any value within each filter
permissions_required: A valid signed-in session; browser developer tools or an API client.
preconditions: 1. You are signed in with developer tools open on the Network tab.
2. Seeded ZZAUTOTEST work orders exist: customer A with an Estimate and an Approved work order, customer B with an Estimate work order.
steps: 1. On the Work Orders page apply Status = Estimate + Approved and Customer = customer A.
2. Capture the resulting list request and response.
expected: 1. One request carries both filters together (both statuses and the customer).
2. The response returns customer A's Estimate and Approved work orders only.
3. Customer B's work orders are absent - the customer filter and status filter both restrict the result, while the two statuses combine as either-or.
spec_ref: requirements.md Story 2 S2-R2; Story 3 S3-R6; Story 8 S8-R3 (backend view)
notes: Endpoint/parameter shape unknown (OQ-7) - VIU-confirm; across-filter AND semantics implied by S8-R3, confirm live.

title: A list request with a deleted or unknown filter value is handled without a server error
permissions_required: A valid signed-in session; browser developer tools or an API client.
preconditions: 1. You are signed in and can replay/edit the work order list request (developer tools or an API client).
2. You have a captured filtered list request, and one of its filter values has since been deleted (for example a removed ZZAUTOTEST customer) or is a made-up identifier.
steps: 1. Send the list request containing the no-longer-existing (or made-up) filter value.
2. Inspect the HTTP status and the response body.
expected: 1. The backend does not fail with a server error (no HTTP 5xx).
2. The response is a normal, successful list response - the invalid value is ignored or simply matches nothing.
3. Any still-valid filter values in the same request are applied normally.
design_ref: requirements.md Story 10 S10-N1; Story 11 S11-R3 (backend view)
notes: Whether the backend ignores the value (returns the rest) or returns an empty match for it is not specified - record the observed behavior at VIU; either is acceptable as long as no error surfaces to the user.

title: A list request with malformed filter parameters does not produce a server error
permissions_required: A valid signed-in session; browser developer tools or an API client.
preconditions: 1. You are signed in and can replay/edit the work order list request.
2. You have a captured filtered list request to tamper with.
steps: 1. Corrupt the filter parameters (wrong types, scrambled values, nonsense text) and send the request.
2. Inspect the HTTP status and the response body.
3. Also open the equally malformed page URL in the browser and watch the page.
expected: 1. The backend responds gracefully - no HTTP 5xx / crash; either a normal (unfiltered or empty) list or a clean validation response.
2. In the browser the page still loads without filters and without an error message, matching the malformed-URL requirement.

title: A filter combination matching nothing returns a successful empty list, not an error
permissions_required: A valid signed-in session; browser developer tools or an API client.
preconditions: 1. You are signed in with developer tools open on the Network tab.
2. A filter combination is known to match no work orders (for example a seeded customer plus a status they never have).
steps: 1. Apply that filter combination on the Work Orders page.
2. Capture the list request and response.
expected: 1. The request succeeds (HTTP 200).
2. The response contains an empty result set (zero work orders) - an empty match is a normal outcome, not an error.
3. The page renders the no-results empty state from this response.
